rules.body:
Apply when a shared source serves distinct visits and attempts, startup can emit synchronously, and decoding can settle later. README.md: "Selecting a file creates a visit. Retry replaces the physical attempt without
opening another visit. Selecting the same file again does open another visit." README.md: "The feed object is shared by attempts and visits for that file. Its `start()`
method may synchronously emit cached data, and `decode(packet)` may return a
value or a Promise." Feed or file identity alone therefore cannot establish visit ownership.

Install the panel listener before starting a source that can synchronously emit cached progress. TASK: "A transfer with a warm progress source shows no initial progress until a later\npacket arrives. Restore the initial progress update without changing the public\ntransfer, retry, navigation, cleanup, audit, or queue-record behavior." The original src/progress.js orders "feed.start();" before "feed.target.addEventListener(\"progress\", listener);"; check and correct that ordering for the panel consumer.

Check originating-visit validity before admitting each packet, including while startup has not returned its cleanup capability. README.md: "One startup window is relevant to this maintenance request: `start()` may emit
more than one packet synchronously. A `showProgress` callback may select or hide
another visit before `start()` returns, while its caller has not yet received
the returned cleanup handle." Logical retirement must therefore prevent subsequent decoding and recording independently of eventual listener removal.

Separate retained history from permission to paint. Already-admitted decoding retains its history output after departure, while painting requires the originating visit to remain current. README.md: "`recordProgress` appends transfer history. `showProgress` paints the panel." src/progress.js: "const deliver = frame => { record(frame); receive(frame); };" src/queue.js: "if (state.current === visit) state.showProgress({ fileId: visit.file.id, attemptId, frame });" Recheck visibility after recording because host callbacks may synchronously navigate.

Track freshness by packet order within the subscription, independently of decode completion order. Record admitted frames while suppressing an older frame's painting after a newer frame has painted; update freshness state before invoking visible callbacks. TASK: "Full\nprogress frames may decode out of order; do not allow an older frame to roll the\ncurrent display backward." This does not authorize numeric comparisons or invented frame-content rules.

Keep the repair scoped to panel progress ordering, admission, and freshness. Preserve retry's captured command and existing record shape: src/retry.js: "// A retry click accepts exactly one command for the current visit and file." src/queue.js: "return { fileId: file.id, attemptId, visitId, kind };" Preserve telemetry's separate startup policy: src/telemetry.js: "// Diagnostics count live deltas only. A cached bootstrap is panel state, not a delta." Do not generalize panel listener-before-start ordering to every consumer or expand queue records.

Verify warm bootstrap and later streaming; reverse decode settlement with retained history and fresh painting; hide, switch, and same-file reopening; and multiple startup packets where the first paint navigates before startup returns. Check rejection of later packets separately from retained settlement of earlier admitted packets. Also check cancellation and detach reentry, retry attribution, telemetry, and independent workspaces. TASK: "Preserve ordinary streaming, diagnostic telemetry,\nand subsequent uses." README.md: "Queue records, notices, cancellation, retry, navigation, and cleanup\nretain their existing behavior." Public examples can exercise these obligations but do not exhaust them.

limitations: These rules apply to the supplied shared-feed, visit-and-attempt ownership model; other ownership or history-retention policies require separate evidence.
The task does not specify decode rejection, thrown callback, malformed-frame, or frame-content comparison policies.

Static review hints and automatic contracts are guidance, not normative evidence. Supplied passing observations demonstrate only those examples; they do not prove causality, exhaustive correctness, or cross-task benefit.
No files were modified, and no scorer, reference implementation, or hidden tests were accessed.

notes: Not approved; visible success or expert summary does not verify effectiveness
